text:
maria: FYI ran a short bring-up for lamaX-8b quant + speculative decode. numbers look promising but theres a small quality blip on codegen prompts. quick thread to sync and decide next steps.
jon: nice! what are the perf gains?
maria: baseline greedy on fp16: 18 req/s per GPU at p95 220ms. with 8-bit quant + speculative two-stage sampler we got 36 req/s and p95 130ms on same machine (A100). ~2x throughput.
kevin: wow that's clean. how deterministic is the sampler? any variability across seeds?
maria: sampler is hybrid: stage1 shallow beam (k=4, early-abort threshold 0.65), stage2 full sampling fallback. we ran 5 seeds, throughput variance <6%, latency p95 stable.
sophia: what about quality metrics? you mentioned a blip on codegen. numbers?
maria: short summary: on commonbench-chat (subset) win-rate vs baseline greedy: ~+0.5% for natural language prompts, but on codegen subset we see -1.8% pass@1 on unit-test check. perplexity on heldout dev set unchanged within noise.
beth: do we have examples of the failing cases? is it hallucination or formatting?
maria: mostly missing trailing newline or slightly different function names -> failing unit tests. not hallucination of facts. small token choice differences early in decode cascade.
jon: could be beam early-abort cutting off the safer path. maybe relax threshold for code tasks.
kevin: quant could also change token ranking subtly. did you compare with quant-aware calibration?
maria: ran two extra runs: 8-bit with QAT-inspired bias-correction (per-channel scale tweak) improved pass@1 to -0.6% (still regressed). removing speculative stage fully (only quant) recovers to parity.
sophia: interesting. so interaction between quantization and speculative early-abort. ops question: are we shipping this config to dedicated pools or experimenting on a canary?
maria: want to canary on dedicated pool with small traffic fraction only if we agree on mitigations. suggestions: 1) code-task routing: route codegen prompts to non-speculative profile, 2) soften early-abort threshold for quantized models, 3) add prompt-aware calibration step.
beth: for (1) do we have a reliable signal to detect codegen at routing level? simple heuristics might work ("```", "def ", "console.") but false positives possible.
jon: we can use a small classifier (embed + logistic) in console to tag codegen vs chat. cheap and deterministic.
maria: I'll stub a classifier and run offline precision/recall on our eval set. if PR > 0.9 we'll route.
kevin: for evaluation methodology, please run: holdout 10k prompts, stratified by task (code/nl/math), run A/B 4k samples live under traffic shadow to measure real-world delta + unit-test harness for code. also add token-level KL and top-1 swap rate between quant and fp16 to quantify token ranking shifts.
eval-bot: scheduled: holdout-run queued (job id: q-98321). will post results when complete.
ops-bot: canary deployment blocked until safety checklist is green. see: https://internal.redwood/safe-deploy-checklist
sophia: timeline?
maria: aiming to run the offline classifier + q-98321 within 48 hours. if regression persists we'll iterate on bias-correction and consider dual-backend routing.
jon: thanks. if you need infra for canary traffic I can allocate a 2-GPU pool for 24h.
maria: yes please @jon, that'd help. I'll post follow-ups with numbers and a short sample of failing cases. :thumbsup:
kevin: also add ablation where we try: (a) 8-bit + no-speculation, (b) 8-bit + speculation relaxed, (c) 6-bit + speculation to see quant depth interactions. small matrix but informative.
maria: added to plan. thanks everyone.
